_about: Hand-chosen, by eye (#7623): for each history the picture on its card and hero (a gallery image from a book the history cites), the concept's word in its original language, the one quote on its card (claim id # source index, a verified claim with a Source Library page), and the excerpt the concept page opens with (an essay and one of its ## sections, or "" for the text before the first ##). scripts/maintenance/concept-history-figures.mjs reads this file and resolves each quote to its printed page; a re-import keeps these choices.

image.alt: Woodcut of a seated Daoist adept with the points of inner alchemy labelled on his body (the Puzhao tu), from the Xingming guizhi, 1615.
image.caption: The Puzhao tu, from the Xingming guizhi (1615)

image.alt: A circular diagram of the soul's states, in concentric rings and radial sections, from Engelbrecht's 1885 edition of Claudianus Mamertus.
image.caption: Diagram of the soul's states, in Claudianus Mamertus, ed. Engelbrecht (1885)

image.alt: Woodcut of six smiths striking an anvil with hammers of different weights, the story of Pythagoras finding the musical ratios, from Gaffurius's Theorica musicae.
image.caption: Pythagoras's smiths, from Gaffurius, Theorica musicae (1480)

image.alt: A horned, winged jinn hovering upside down over a sleeping man, a painted page from the Kitab al-Bulhan.
image.caption: A jinn over a sleeper, from the Kitab al-Bulhan (c. 1400)

image.alt: Woodcut of a Dominican friar holding a quill and a model church, in Tomás de Mercado's Summa de tratos y contratos.
image.caption: A Dominican friar, in Mercado, Summa de tratos y contratos (1571)

image.alt: Kepler's engraving of the planetary spheres nested between the five regular solids, from the Mysterium cosmographicum.
image.caption: Kepler's nested solids, from the Mysterium cosmographicum

image.alt: Ani and his wife before the door of the tomb, with the ba, a human-headed bird, flying above, from the Papyrus of Ani.
image.caption: The ba over the tomb door, from the Papyrus of Ani, ed. Budge (1913)

image.alt: Engraving of people dancing to a fiddler to cure a tarantula bite, from Kircher's Phonurgia nova.
image.caption: Dancing out the tarantula's bite, from Kircher, Phonurgia nova (1673)
